_signoff: One block is NOT verified: `defective`. v1.8 says defective gear may be replaced or refunded after inspection and that customized items are returnable if defective, and it says nothing about a warranty period or who pays return shipping when the fault is ours. That gap is stated on the page as a chip rather than filled in. Cole owns it.
headline: Sixty days on a club
lede: Play the putter. Hit one wedge on a mat. If the club doesn't earn its place in the bag, tell us inside sixty days and send it back. Apparel and gear get thirty, and the conditions are tighter because a worn shirt can't be sold twice.

sections.title: How long you have
sections.lede: The clock starts the day it lands, not the day you ordered.

items.v: 60 days from delivery. Wedges, putters and hybrids.
30 days from delivery. Polos and hats.
30 days from delivery. Covers, grips, gloves, tees.
Final sale, unless it arrives defective.

paras: A request made after the window closes is not accepted, and the window is per category — sixty days is a club thing, and buying a polo alongside a wedge does not extend the polo.

Buying ahead for a birthday or Christmas is worth a note here. The window runs from delivery, so a club bought in November and handed over in December has spent most of its sixty days sitting in a closet. If that is the plan, it is worth telling us when you order rather than after the window has gone.
sections.note: One golfer told us exactly this in a review — the gift arrived long before the return window mattered to him. It is a fair complaint and the reason this paragraph exists.

sections.title: Starting a return
sections.lede: Clubs and everything else go two different ways. Sending a club back without doing this first is the one mistake that cannot be undone.

paras: Contact us before you send anything. Every club return needs approval first, and approval needs photos — that is how the condition is agreed before the club is in a box rather than argued about after.
Email support@luckygolf.com or open the chat on the site. Tell us the order number, which club, and what is wrong with it, and attach photos of the face and the sole.
A club that turns up without authorization is not accepted. There is no way to process it and no record that it is coming.
These go through the Returns Portal, or through the instructions that came with your order confirmation. No approval call, no photos — just the portal.
If you cannot find the confirmation email, chat or email will point you at it.

tbd.label: Needs confirming
tbd.text: the Returns Portal's address, so this page can link straight to it instead of describing it.
tbd.ask: Until it is confirmed, the order confirmation email is the reliable route.

sections.nav: What you can do with a club first
sections.title: What you can do with it first
sections.lede: Sixty days is only worth having if you can actually use the club, so the conditions differ by what the club is for.

paras: Use it. That is the point of sixty days on a putter, and a putter you have not rolled is a putter you cannot judge.

To come back it has to be in brand-new condition: no face marks, no sole wear, no scratches, dents, chips, bag chatter or grip wear. No regripping, bending, cutting or altering — a modified putter is not returnable at all.
One wedge per order may be opened and tested, on a turf mat or another non-abrasive surface. Any others stay factory sealed.
The one you tested comes back with no groove wear, no face marks, no sole wear and no cosmetic or structural damage. Off a mat, that is achievable. Off a range floor or out of a bunker, it is not.
These have to appear completely unused — no visible wear, no damage, no modifications.

sections.note: Wear beyond these conditions means a partial refund or a declined return, judged on what turns up.

sections.title: Apparel
sections.lede: Thirty days, and it has to come back the way it went out.

items: All original tags still attached. A return without its tags has $7 deducted from the refund.
No makeup or deodorant marks, no odors, no pet hair, no stretching, no laundering.
Requests after thirty days are not accepted.

paras: Size is the reason most apparel comes back, which is why the size guide sits on the size picker itself rather than three sections down the page. Thirty seconds there saves a shipping label.

sections.title: Gear and accessories
paras: Covers, grips, gloves and tees come back unused and undamaged. Anything showing wear or use is not eligible.
A grip that has been fitted to a shaft counts as used. Grips are the one item where this catches people out — once it is on the club, it is yours.
Something that arrives defective may be replaced or refunded after inspection.

sections.title: Refunds, and who pays what

items.v: After the item is received and inspected. Not when it is posted, and not when tracking says delivered.
The customer's. We do not send a prepaid label.
Possible where an item comes back outside the stated conditions.

paras: Inspection is the step people underestimate. The refund is raised once the item is in front of someone, so the useful thing to send us is the tracking number for the return — it is what tells us to go looking for it.

sections.title: If it arrives damaged, or breaks
sections.lede: This is not a return. Tell us and we deal with it.
paras: A club that turns up damaged, or that fails in normal use, is a different conversation from one you have simply decided against. Email support@luckygolf.com or open the chat, with photos and the order number, and do not send it anywhere until we have answered.
What is settled: defective gear may be replaced or refunded after inspection, and a customized item — final sale in every other circumstance — is returnable if it arrives defective.

tbd.label: Needs confirming
tbd.text: the warranty period on a club, and who pays return shipping when the fault is ours rather than a change of mind.
tbd.ask: Both are real questions golfers have asked us and neither has an answer written down yet, so this page does not pretend to one. Ask and we will sort it out case by case in the meantime.

sections.title: When a return is refused
sections.lede: Five reasons, all of them avoidable, and all of them easier to avoid than to appeal.

items: Visible wear or damage beyond the conditions above.
The item has been modified — regripped, bent, cut, altered.
It is outside the return window.
It is missing the required approval or documentation.
It was sent back without authorization.

paras: The first four are judgement calls we would rather make with you before the club ships than after it arrives. The fifth is not a judgement call: ask first.
